title: The Last Oath Revisited
premise: When the border wards between Thornfell and the fae realm of Hollowmere collapse on the night the stars vanish, Silas Blackwood discovers his runaway apprenticeship was no accident: his former mistress, the hedge-witch Maren, bound him at birth as the living keystone of the covenant. Hunted by both a corrupt human regent who wants the wards rebuilt as a weapon and a Hollowmere court that wants them shattered forever, Silas must gather three scattered oath-stones and choose which truth to swear. In the end, he reforges the covenant not as a wall but as a bridge, sacrificing his own magic and his memory of Maren to seal it, ending the long winter but exiling himself from both realms.
about_author: E. M. Thackeray is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction. They write fantasy rooted in borders, weather, and the bargains people make to survive both.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Silas smuggles iron-warded goods through the Thornfell passes when the stars vanish and every ward along the border dies at once. A dying courier presses an oath-stone into his hands with Maren's name on his lips. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: dread and reluctant responsibility as the safe, lawless life he built collapses around him.

chapters.title: What Maren Never Taught Me
chapters.summary: Silas flees to Maren's cottage seeking answers, finding it ransacked and her gone, leaving only a journal hinting he was 'the keystone.' Regent's soldiers arrive hunting the stone; Silas escapes using smuggler routes only he knows. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into questions—was his whole childhood a lie?

chapters.title: The Court of Hollow Bells
chapters.summary: Crossing into Hollowmere to find answers, Silas is captured by Lady Vesperine's court, who reveal the covenant bound two realms in mutual survival—and that someone inside the court broke it. She offers alliance if he retrieves the second stone from the drowned chapel. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: wary fascination; the enemy is not what he expected.

chapters.title: Drowned Chapel, Rising Water
chapters.summary: With the fae scout Bramble-ashe as reluctant guide, Silas dives the flooded chapel for the second stone while the long winter's first true freeze seals the lake above them. He learns the stones answer to oaths kept, not power held. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into first real courage.

chapters.title: The Regent's Bargain
chapters.summary: Captured by Regent Aldous Crane, Silas learns the regent engineered the wards' fall to rebuild them as a one-way weapon against Hollowmere. Crane offers Silas legitimacy, safety, and Maren's location—in exchange for the stones. POV: alternating Silas and Crane. Emotional beat: temptation; the offer would fix everything except his conscience.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Hedge-Witch
chapters.summary: Escaping Crane's fortress, Silas finds Maren imprisoned and dying, having spent her magic shielding him since birth. She confesses the binding was her choice, made out of love, and gives him the third stone and her forgiveness. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grief and reconciliation; loyalty and truth finally align.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: The unnatural winter reaches full force; villages starve on both sides of the dead border. Silas, Vesperine, and Bramble-ashe race to the covenant site at Thornfell's peak while Crane marches an army to seize it. POV: rotating among Silas, Vesperine, and a starving villager. Emotional beat: mounting desperation as time runs out.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Peak
chapters.summary: At the covenant site, Bramble-ashe is revealed as the court traitor who broke the wards, believing severance would free Hollowmere from dependence on humans. Vesperine confronts him as Crane's army arrives below. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: heartbreak—the betrayer was his friend, and his grievance is not entirely wrong.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Climax: Silas refuses both Crane's weapon-covenant and Bramble-ashe's severance, instead swearing a new oath as bridge rather than barrier. The stones demand a price equal to the binding: his magic and his memories of Maren. Crane falls to his own broken wards; Bramble-ashe kneels. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: sacrifice freely chosen, terrible and luminous.

chapters.title: A Bridge Between Realms
chapters.summary: Spring returns to both realms under a new open-border covenant. Silas, magicless and memory-hollow, cannot cross either threshold—but both peoples build him a cottage at the pass itself, keeper of the bridge he forged. A stranger leaves flowers at his door; he doesn't know why he weeps. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace; the price paid, and worth it.
